key_insight: Introduce a scalable variational inference framework for stochastic differential equations driven by Lévy processes by using a learnable "neural tilting" change-of-measure on the jump (Lévy) part, enabling accurate Bayesian inference for models with jumps and heavy tails that were previously intractable or non-scalable.
problem_solved: Existing Bayesian inference for Lévy-driven SDEs is either computationally expensive (Monte Carlo) or inaccurate/non-scalable (standard neural variational methods). This work provides a practical, scalable method to perform posterior inference for SDEs with jumps and heavy-tailed noise.
method: Define a variational family via a tilting (change-of-measure) of the Lévy jump distribution, parameterized by neural networks — "neural tilting" — to flexibly capture posterior behavior of jumps.

Optimize a tractable variational objective (ELBO or tilted surrogate) using amortized neural inference and SDE solvers, combining probabilistic rigor of importance/tilting with scalability of deep learning.
Use design choices (e.g., stable reweighting, efficient simulation of tilted jump measures) to make training numerically stable and computationally efficient for practical datasets.
impact: Makes principled Bayesian modeling of jumps and heavy tails practical at scale, improving uncertainty quantification and robustness in domains like finance, climate modeling, and safety-critical AI where extreme events matter.
visual_elements: Schematic diagram: SDE sample paths comparison (Gaussian diffusion vs Lévy-driven with jumps) to highlight jump behavior and heavy tails.
Method flowchart: data → neural tilting module (learnable change-of-measure) → tilted SDE simulator → variational training loop (ELBO), showing end-to-end pipeline.
Performance chart: accuracy vs compute (or RMSE/ELBO vs runtime) comparing Monte Carlo, standard VI, and neural-tilting VI to show scalability/accuracy trade-offs.
Domain icons: small panels showing applications (finance, climate, autonomous systems) annotated with benefits (better tail risk, extreme-event capture).
paper_title: Variational Inference for Lévy Process-Driven SDEs via Neural Tilting
paper_authors: Yaman Kindap, Manfred Opper, Benjamin Dupuis, Umut Simsekli, Tolga Birdal
